problem: VLN agents trained on small human-annotated datasets (R2R 14K, RxR 79K instructions in 61 Matterport3D train scenes) struggle with complex language grounding and spatial language. Pretraining on web image-text or text corpora gives only limited gains. Prior synthetic-instruction augmentation (e.g., the Speaker model) was both low quality (instructions poorly grounded and mostly unfollowable by humans) and small scale.
motivation: Wayfinding needs spatially grounded, action-oriented language: egocentric and allocentric relations, verbs, negations, and 'until' conditions. Such language is rare in static image-text data and hard to ground from text alone. The recent Marky generator produces near-human-quality instructions, and Gibson's 500+ scanned environments sit unused for VLN only because they lack navigation graphs. Large-scale in-domain synthetic data plus simple, high-throughput imitation learning might therefore outperform RL-heavy agents.
key_idea: Scale in-domain VLN training data by two orders of magnitude (4.2M instruction-trajectory pairs), using Marky-generated multilingual instructions in Matterport3D plus 491 newly auto-graphed Gibson environments and SE3DS-synthesized novel-viewpoint panoramas, and train a plain mT5-style transformer agent purely with imitation learning (behavioral cloning + DAgger).
insight: Instruction quality matters more than quantity or mixing. In pretraining, Marky instructions add +27 SR on RxR val-unseen over human data alone, whereas Speaker instructions add only +2 (Table 2, row 4 vs 1). Adding Speaker data on top of Marky actually hurts (row 3 vs 4; row 8 vs 9). Scaling to new environments still pays off: Gibson adds +11 SR on RxR and +12 on R2R (row 6 vs 3). SE3DS novel views help without Gibson (+6 SR on RxR, row 5 vs 3) but give ~0 on RxR once Gibson is added (row 7 vs 6), since new environments already add viewpoint diversity. mT5-large adds +2 SR over base. With enough data, pure IL beats IL+RL agents. The main remaining gap is error recovery: MARVAL makes fewer first mistakes than human followers yet reaches the goal far less often (SR 64.8 vs 94.5). Synthetic data is domain-dependent: Marky was trained on RxR, and the agent is not SOTA on R2R.
method: Gibson navigation graphs: a RedNet (ResNet-50, RGB-D) model trained on Matterport3D panos predicts navigable directions in 8x16x5 pitch/heading/distance buckets. An edge is added if (λd·geodesic/Euclidean − λp·p_edge ≤ 1), distance ≤ 3.5 m and |Δz| ≤ 3 m (geodesic from Habitat). The result is OR-ed with a minimum spanning tree for connectivity; λ's are grid-searched on MP3D val (F1 0.70).

Marky-Gibson data: sample 3 panos, use a TSP solver for the shortest path visiting all 3, and discard paths longer than 40 m or 16 steps, with at most 3K paths per environment. This gives 1.06M paths (avg 7.1 steps, 19.3 m) in 491 Gibson train+val environments, annotated with 3.2M Marky instructions in en/hi/te. Combined with Marky-Matterport (1M) this totals 4.2M pairs.

SE3DS view synthesis: 200 variations of each Matterport environment. In each variation a pano is spatially perturbed by up to 1.5 m with 50% probability and re-rendered by an image-to-image GAN; variations are randomly sampled during training.

MARVAL agent: a non-autoregressive mT5 transformer encoder trained from scratch. It fully attends over instruction WordPieces, the history (each past pano compressed to one vector by a separate transformer with mean pooling, added to the chosen action), the current 36-view pano and the action candidates plus STOP. It adds learned pairwise modality attention biases. Image features are frozen 640-d MURAL-large (EfficientNet-B7) features with learned absolute and relative direction embeddings.

Pretraining losses: masked language modeling (15% span masking), progress prediction (20 bins from the CLS token), constrained action classification over the candidates, and unconstrained prediction over 36 directions + STOP. Constrained and unconstrained logits are summed equally at inference (+1-2% accuracy).

Finetuning on human data (RxR or R2R): only the WordPiece embeddings are updated, with the transformer frozen. Training is behavioral cloning followed by one DAgger iteration. The DAgger expert returns the next GT step if on the path; otherwise the shortest path to the goal (if the GT is a shortest path) or back to the nearest GT node.
Optional pre-exploration: sample paths in Val-Unseen/Test environments, label them with Marky, and add them to training (self-training without human labels).

setting.backbone: MARVAL: mT5-large-architecture transformer encoder trained from scratch (no text/image-text pretraining), on frozen precomputed MURAL-large (EfficientNet-B7) image features
setting.model_size: mT5-large (parameter count not stated; mT5-base used in most ablations)
setting.training_data: Pretraining on R2R + RxR human data, Marky-Matterport (1M instructions, 61 MP3D envs), Marky-Gibson (3.2M instructions on 1.06M paths in 491 Gibson envs) and SE3DS-synthesized novel-view panos (200 variations per env). About 4.2M synthetic instruction-trajectory pairs; 5.14M iterations at batch 128 (>650M steps of experience, >700M including finetuning). Speaker-Matterport (178K) was tested but excluded from the best model. Finetuning uses the RxR or R2R human data with BC + DAgger.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, 12 headings x 3 elevations) as frozen MURAL features with direction embeddings
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (plus Gibson panos with auto-generated nav graphs; Habitat used only to compute geodesics for graph building)
setting.privileged: none for the main results; the Pre-Explore variant uses Marky-labeled paths sampled in the evaluation (Val-Unseen/Test) environments

numbers_note: Tables are complete. Additional results not listed above: pretraining-data ablations with mT5-base/large (Table 2 val-unseen, Table 5 val-seen; e.g., base with all data incl. SE3DS: RxR val-unseen SR 55.9 / nDTW 65.1). Per-language RxR val results (Table 6; e.g., hi-IN val-unseen SR 65.85, nDTW 72.02). The first-error analysis is given only in a figure. The paper is internally inconsistent on Gibson trajectory counts (abstract/intro say 3.2M trajectories; the data section says 1.3M or 1.06M paths with 3.2M instructions).
results: On RxR, MARVAL trained purely with imitation learning sets a new SOTA over RL-trained agents. On test it reaches nDTW 66.8 / SR 60.7 / SDTW 53.5 vs EnvEdit (3-agent ensemble) 64.6 / 60.4 / 51.8. On val-seen it reaches nDTW 79.1 vs 71.1, and on val-unseen SR 64.8 / nDTW 70.8 vs 62.8 / 68.5. Pre-exploration with Marky instructions in the test environments lifts test nDTW to 68.6. On R2R it is strong but not SOTA: test SR 62 / SPL 58 vs EnvEdit 68 / 64 and HAMT 65 / 60, which the authors attribute to Marky being trained on RxR-style instructions.
limitations: The synthetic instructions are domain-dependent: Marky was trained on RxR, so gains do not carry over to R2R (not SOTA). Retraining Marky on R2R is hampered by R2R lacking pose traces.
Gains over SOTA are much larger in seen environments (+8 nDTW) than in unseen test environments (+2). The agent rarely recovers after its first error (SR 64.8 vs human 94.5).

Requires massive compute (5.14M iterations, >700M steps), internal Google components (MURAL features, Marky) and the discrete nav-graph setting. The authors report that training existing agents such as HAMT on the full 4.2M set is infeasible without re-engineering.
